nodes.label: Mistake: Assumed ratio exports were independent
nodes.rationale: Treated 12 exports as separate files. They were copy-paste duplicates. One bug became 12 bugs. Should have refactored before fixing.

nodes.label: Mistake: Safety logic without explicit spec

nodes.label: Mistake: Trusted float equality

nodes.label: Mistake: No regression safety net

nodes.label: Mistake: Rotation bias invisible

nodes.label: Mistake: Scattered params

nodes.label: Silent degradation is unacceptable
nodes.notes: Inherited from ARS. Every failure mode in the TV→WunderTrading→Exchange pipeline must surface explicitly via logs, alerts, or dashboards. A bot that silently stops trading is worse than one that errors loudly.

nodes.label: Test-then-integrate
nodes.notes: Build standalone, validate against real data, then fold into live. Never go live with a strategy that hasn't run paper for ≥2 weeks. Same discipline as ARS development.

nodes.label: Realistic costs from day one
nodes.notes: Every backtest uses slippage=3 ticks, commission=0.1%. If the edge doesn't survive these, it's not real. No exception, even for promising strategies.

nodes.label: One change at a time
nodes.notes: When live, change only one variable per session: position size OR strategy version OR exchange — never two at once. Otherwise you cannot attribute results to causes.

nodes.label: Small first, scale on proof
nodes.notes: First live deployment uses 10–20% of target position size. Scale only after ≥2 weeks of clean live execution matching paper P&L within 20%.

nodes.label: 📅 Phase 0 — Decisions before code
nodes.notes:
Goal: lock all architectural decisions in Week 1 so Phases 1–5 don't get derailed.

Exit: strategy selection locked, exchange chosen, KYC done, TradingView tier confirmed, WunderTrading account created.

Time: 8–12h active over ~1 calendar week (KYC runs in parallel).

nodes.label: Re-run all 11 strategies with realistic costs
nodes.notes:
For each Pine strategy: slippage=3, commission_value=0.1, fill_orders_on_standard_ohlc=true. Record net profit, profit factor, max DD, total trades, Sharpe.

Drill down to backtest sub-canvas for scientific-method detail.

nodes.label: Select 1–3 strategies for first deployment
nodes.notes: Criteria: profit factor ≥1.3 after costs, max DD ≤25%, ≥100 trades, type diversity. User leaning: FIB BTC first.

nodes.label: Choose exchange — Bybit / Binance / HyperLiquid
nodes.notes: Bybit = best WT integration. Binance = most liquid. HyperLiquid = WT premium FREE + lowest fees but DEX risks. See Library for review.

nodes.label: Confirm TradingView tier (Premium already active)
nodes.notes: User has TV Premium ~1.5 years. 400 non-expiring alerts. No upgrade.

nodes.label: Create exchange account + trade-only API key
nodes.notes: API permissions: TRADE only, NO withdrawal. Bybit/Binance KYC may take 1–3 days. HyperLiquid = no KYC. Start KYC Day 1.

nodes.label: Create WunderTrading account (Free tier)
nodes.notes: Free tier supports webhooks + 2 bots. Sufficient for paper phase and for 1–2 live strategies.

nodes.label: ⛔ Blocker: Exchange KYC delay (1–3 days)
nodes.notes: Mitigation: start KYC Day 1, parallel with backtest work. Fall back to HyperLiquid (no KYC) if Bybit/Binance stalls past Day 5.

nodes.label: ✅ Exit: All decisions locked, accounts created
nodes.notes:
Phase 0 complete when:
• Top 3 strategies chosen and documented
• Exchange account live with API key
• WunderTrading account created
• TradingView Premium confirmed (already done)
• Backtest validation sub-canvas complete

nodes.label: 🛠️ Phase 1 — Webhook-ready cleanup
nodes.notes:
Goal: transform selected Pine strategies from backtest-only to webhook-ready. Most code-intensive phase.

Exit: all strategies pass no-repaint audit, alert messages fire correctly in TV log, JSON validated, 24h dry-run on chart with alerts enabled.

Time: 4–8h × 3 strategies = 12–24h active. Calendar: 2 weeks.

nodes.label: Audit calc_on_every_tick + process_orders_on_close
nodes.notes:
Both must be set so signals fire only on bar close:
  calc_on_every_tick = false
  process_orders_on_close = false

nodes.label: Audit request.security() for repainting
nodes.notes:
Every request.security() needs:
  _src[1] (use previous bar)
  lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on

Without these, HTF data repaints silently in real-time.

nodes.label: Add barstate.isconfirmed guard to entries
nodes.notes:
Wrap entry conditions:
  if myCondition and barstate.isconfirmed
      strategy.entry(...)

Guarantees bar is closed before alert fires.

nodes.label: Add alert_message JSON to every entry/close
nodes.notes:
WunderTrading expects JSON in alert message:
  {"code":"Enter-Long","orderType":"market","amountPerTradeType":"quote","amountPerTrade":100,"leverage":1}

Codes (case-sensitive!): Enter-Long, Enter-Short, Exit-Long, Exit-Short, Exit-All.

In TV alert message field use {{strategy.order.alert_message}}.

nodes.label: Remove strategy.exit() TP/SL — set in WunderTrading
nodes.notes: TP/SL via TV alerts has webhook latency (3–10s). Set TP/SL directly in WT bot config — exchange-side orders, sub-second execution. Last-resort safety net even if webhook pipeline fails.

nodes.label: 24h dry-run: enable alerts, watch the alert log
nodes.notes: Per strategy: apply to chart, enable alerts to 'Once Per Bar Close', notification = popup only (no webhook yet). After 24h verify alert log matches strategy plot markers.

nodes.label: Use Claude Code for cleanup (~50% time saving)
nodes.notes: Claude Code is well-suited to: adding alert_message JSON, auditing request.security() calls, refactoring exit logic. Estimate: 12–24h → 6–15h with Claude Code assistance.

nodes.label: ✅ Exit: 3 strategies webhook-ready, dry-run clean
nodes.notes:
Phase 1 complete when:
• All chosen strategies pass no-repaint audit
• alert_message JSON present on every order
• 24h dry-run shows alert log matches chart signals
• TP/SL moved to WunderTrading bot config

nodes.label: 🧪 Phase 2 — Paper deploy on WunderTrading
nodes.notes:
Goal: validate full pipeline (TV → webhook → WunderTrading → exchange paper) with zero real money. Purpose is NOT to re-confirm profitability — it's to prove plumbing works.

Exit: 0 webhook delivery failures for ≥2 consecutive weeks, ≥20–30 paper trades, win rate within 10% of backtest, 0 position desyncs.

Time: 4–6h setup + 30 min/day × 3–4 weeks. ~10h active.

nodes.label: Connect exchange API key (paper mode)
nodes.notes: Settings → My Exchanges → Add New → select exchange → paste API Key + Secret → enable PAPER TRADING mode. Verify WT shows paper balance.

nodes.label: Create Signal Bot per strategy
nodes.notes: Bots → Signal Bot → Create Bot. Configure pair, position size, leverage, TP/SL, Multiple entries OFF. Free tier covers 2 bots.

nodes.label: Wire TradingView alerts to webhook URL
nodes.notes: TV → Create Alert. Condition = strategy. Trigger = 'alert() function calls only'. Message = {{strategy.order.alert_message}}. Notifications tab → Webhook URL: paste from WT bot.

nodes.label: Verify first signal arrives in WunderTrading log
nodes.notes: Monitor: TV alert log (signal fired?) → WT bot log (signal received?) → paper account (position opened?). If TV fires but WT doesn't show → webhook delivery failure (often 3-second TV timeout).

nodes.label: Daily reconciliation: TV count vs WT count vs position
nodes.notes:
Single biggest reliability risk: missed webhooks. Catch by comparing daily counts:
• N alerts fired in TV log
• N signals received in WT
• Open position matches strategy chart

Any mismatch = silent failure.

nodes.label: Test through ≥1 high-volatility move
nodes.notes: Webhook reliability degrades during volatility. Don't go live until you've watched paper survive at least one 3%+ move. Compare paper fill timing to actual market timing — gap >10s on 15-min strategy = OK; >60s = concerning.

nodes.label: ⛔ Blocker: TV alert reliability under load
nodes.notes:
Known limitation: TradingView's 3-second webhook timeout means alerts can be silently dropped during high-volume periods.

Mitigation: 15-min+ timeframes (latency invisible). Monitor delivery counts daily.

nodes.label: ✅ Exit: 0 failures × 2 weeks, 20+ paper trades
nodes.notes:
Phase 2 complete when:
• ≥14 consecutive days, 0 webhook failures
• ≥20–30 paper trades end-to-end
• Win rate within 10% of backtest
• 0 position desyncs detected
• Survived ≥1 high-volatility period

nodes.label: 🛡️ Phase 3 — Risk controls + monitoring
nodes.notes:
Goal: build safety infrastructure before any real money. Runs parallel with second half of Phase 2.

Exit: 3 kill switches tested, Telegram bot sending notifications, daily P&L monitoring operational, position-sizing math documented.

Time: 8–12h active over 2 weeks.

nodes.label: Kill switch L1: Pine equity-based auto-flatten
nodes.notes:
Add to each strategy:
  if strategy.equity < strategy.initial_capital * 0.85
      strategy.close_all()

Fires webhook to flatten if equity drops 15% from initial. First line of defense.

nodes.label: Kill switch L2: WunderTrading bot pause
nodes.notes: Document procedure: WT dashboard → bot → Pause. Practice doing it in <30s. What you reach for if a strategy misbehaves but equity-trigger hasn't fired yet.

nodes.label: Kill switch L3: Exchange API key disable
nodes.notes: Last resort: disable API key on exchange. Stops ALL bot trading instantly regardless of webhook state. Bookmark the API key page.

nodes.label: Position sizing formula (1% risk × leverage)
nodes.notes: Risk per trade = 1% × held capital. Leverage scales the deployable capital. First live: cut to 0.5% risk for extra caution.

nodes.label: Build Telegram alert bot (~4–8h, Claude Code-friendly)
nodes.notes: Python with python-telegram-bot. Receives WT notifications + sends daily P&L summary. Claude Code can scaffold in ~2h. Deploy as cron job or systemd service. Telegram Bot API is free.

nodes.label: Daily reconciliation script (exchange vs WT vs expected)
nodes.notes:
Cron job that checks 3 numbers daily:
• Exchange account balance
• WT reported balance
• Expected balance (initial + cum P&L)

Any mismatch = position desync. Pings Telegram immediately.

nodes.label: ✅ Exit: 3 kill switches tested, monitoring live
nodes.notes:
Phase 3 complete when:
• All 3 kill switch levels tested in paper
• Telegram bot delivering trade notifications
• Daily reconciliation cron job active
• Position-sizing math written down and tested

nodes.label: 🚀 Phase 4 — Small live rollout
nodes.notes:
Goal: go live with Strategy #1 at 10–20% of intended capital. #2 and #3 stay on paper. Compare live to paper.

Exit: Strategy #1 live ≥2 weeks, live P&L within 20% of paper, 0 position desyncs, 0 webhook failures.

Time: 4–6h setup + 30 min/day × 2 weeks. ~10h active.

nodes.label: Switch Strategy #1 from paper to live API
nodes.notes: WT bot config → swap paper exchange for real exchange API. Position size = 10–20% of target. Verify first live trade fills correctly: fill price, size, fees vs expectation.

nodes.label: Watch first 48h like a hawk
nodes.notes:
Daily checks: every fill matches strategy intent, no duplicates, no partial fill desync, Telegram bot delivering all notifications.

If anything looks off → kill switch immediately, investigate.

nodes.label: After 1 week clean → deploy Strategy #2
nodes.notes: Gate: Strategy #1 must have ≥7 days clean live AND P&L within 20% of paper before adding #2. Same procedure: switch to live API, 10–20% size, watch closely.

nodes.label: Strategy #3: keep paper unless #1 + #2 stable
nodes.notes: Conservative: only deploy #3 if both #1 and #2 are running cleanly. Better to hit June 30 with 2 live + 1 paper than 3 live + chaos.

nodes.label: Compare live vs paper P&L weekly
nodes.notes:
Weekly: live P&L vs what paper would have done same period. Slippage analysis: avg fill vs avg signal price. Fee drag: actual fees as % of P&L.

Drift >20% = investigate (slippage, missed alerts, size mismatch).

nodes.label: Silent failure modes catalogue (drill-down)
nodes.notes: Sub-canvas: 6 known silent failure modes with detection method for each. Click portal arrow ↗ to drill down.

nodes.label: ⛔ Blocker: emotional override of the system
nodes.notes: Biggest Phase 4 risk isn't technical — it's overriding the system manually. Don't manual-trade on the same sub-account. Don't edit live strategies without pausing the bot first.

nodes.label: ✅ Exit: live ≥2 wks, P&L within 20% of paper
nodes.notes:
Phase 4 complete when:
• Strategy #1 live ≥2 weeks, clean
• Live P&L within 20% of paper expectation
• 0 position desyncs detected
• All risk controls fired correctly when triggered

nodes.label: 📈 Phase 5 — Scale & stabilize → June 30 deadline
nodes.notes:
Goal: scale to target sizes on proven strategies. Deploy additional strategies if pipeline is stable. Document for ongoing operations. HIT JUNE 30 with 1–3 strategies live.

Exit: 1–3 strategies live on real capital, executing autonomously, monitoring operational, runbook written.

nodes.label: Scale Strategy #1 to target size if performing
nodes.notes: If Wk 7–9 live performance matches paper within 20%, scale Strategy #1 from 10–20% to full target size. One step, then watch 24h.

nodes.label: Deploy Strategy #2 to live (if not already)
nodes.notes: Same procedure as #1 in Phase 4: switch to live API, start at 10–20%, scale after 1 week of clean execution.

nodes.label: Evaluate Strategy #3
nodes.notes: Deploy #3 only if #1 + #2 are both stable. If pipeline shows fragility, hit June 30 with 2 strategies live and #3 still on paper. Better to land safely than overreach.

nodes.label: Write the operations runbook
nodes.notes: Document daily checks (10 min), weekly checks (30 min), monthly checks (1h), how to restart bots, how to handle each known failure mode, where the kill switches are. Hand it to your future self.

nodes.label: Final reconciliation: exchange vs WT vs expected
nodes.notes: Full audit: exchange balance + WT reported balance + P&L expected from logs. All three agree within rounding. Document what's live.

nodes.label: 🎯 June 30 milestone: 1–3 strategies live
nodes.notes:
Hard deadline. Definition of done:
• 1–3 strategies live on real capital via WunderTrading
• Executing autonomously, no manual intervention
• Monitoring + kill switches operational
• Runbook written and tested

nodes.label: TradingView Premium = $0 (already paid)
nodes.notes: User has TV Premium ~1.5 years. Cost is sunk. 400 non-expiring alerts available — sufficient for entire roadmap.

nodes.label: Exchange account = $0
nodes.notes: Free on Bybit, Binance, HyperLiquid. Trading fees apply per trade (Bybit ~0.10% taker, HyperLiquid ~0.045% taker).

nodes.label: WunderTrading Free = $0 (paper + 1–2 live)
nodes.notes: Free tier covers webhooks + 2 bots. Sufficient for entire paper phase AND for going live with up to 2 strategies.

nodes.label: HyperLiquid bonus: WT premium FREE
nodes.notes: If exchange = HyperLiquid, ALL WunderTrading premium features are free (verified Apr 2026). Eliminates the $19.95–$89.95/mo WT cost entirely.

nodes.label: WunderTrading Basic = $19.95/mo (3 live)
nodes.notes: Upgrade trigger: deploying a 3rd live strategy. Basic tier = 5 bots, 15 open positions, trailing stops. Skip if staying at 1–2 strategies.

nodes.label: Final exchange — Bybit, Binance, or HyperLiquid?
nodes.notes: Bybit = best WT integration. Binance = most liquid. HyperLiquid = free WT premium + lowest fees but DEX risks. Decide before Phase 1.

nodes.label: Strategy #1 confirmed = FIB BTC?
nodes.notes: User leaning: FIB BTC. Final confirmation pending Phase 0 backtest re-run with realistic costs. If FIB BTC fails profit-factor ≥1.3, fall back to next candidate.

nodes.label: Strategies #2 and #3 = TBD post-backtest
nodes.notes: From the 11: FIB LONGS/SHORTS, LIQ SWEEP LONGS/SHORTS, BREAKOUT LONGS/SHORTS, RSI DIV, EMA TOUCH, NQ 15M RANGE, BTC 15M RANGE, GC IB. Pick for diversity (different assets, different strategy types).

nodes.label: If HyperLiquid: comfortable with USDC-only collateral?
nodes.notes: HL requires USDC as collateral, deposited from another chain (Arbitrum etc.). Means: bridging step + only USDC margin (no BTC/ETH as collateral). Practical for crypto strategies.

nodes.label: May exam load — does Wk 4–5 capacity drop?
nodes.notes: User confirmed 7–10h/wk realistic. Discrete Math exam Apr 28 (end of Phase 1). May exam schedule TBD. If May has heavy exams, slow Phase 2 (mostly observation, 30 min/day).

nodes.label: Pre-mortem: what's the one thing most likely to break this plan?
nodes.notes: Most common retail algo failure: paper testing too short, going live during low-vol period, then losing trust when vol returns. Mitigation: insist on 'survive ≥1 high-vol move' Phase 2 exit criterion.

nodes.notes:

nodes.label: Self-hosted FastAPI webhook receiver
nodes.notes:
Deferred to LATER (Oct 2026+). 25–48h to build production-grade. WunderTrading eliminates this entire workstream.

Build trigger: when WT $19.95+/mo matters relative to Hetzner €3.49/mo, OR when you need cross-strategy correlation limits / custom dynamic sizing.

nodes.label: VPS deployment
nodes.notes: Not needed for June. WT's managed infrastructure more reliable than solo VPS for first deployment. Worthwhile only when self-hosted receiver is built. Cheapest viable: Hetzner CX11, €3.49/mo.

nodes.label: ARS / APR Systems-branch live deployment
nodes.notes: Both still in validation. ARS at v6.3.1 with OOS Sharpe ~0.01. APR in Phase 1 (debug layer). Both feature-frozen pending validation. Cannot deploy live until their own roadmap milestones complete.

nodes.label: Trinity Allocator (Safe ARS + Risky ARS + APR)
nodes.notes: Parked behind ARS validation. Multi-strategy portfolio allocation is a future phase, not a June-30 phase.

nodes.label: QuantConnect / Alpaca migration
nodes.notes: No benefit for crypto execution on Bybit/Binance/HyperLiquid. These platforms excel for US equities/options. Defer unless Algorithms branch expands to US markets.

nodes.label: MQL5 / MetaTrader port
nodes.notes: No value. Pine + WunderTrading handles execution. MQL5 is MetaTrader-specific, doesn't connect to crypto exchanges.

nodes.label: AWS / co-location for latency optimization
nodes.notes: Irrelevant at 15-min to 4-hour timeframes. Latency matters at sub-second execution. A 3-second webhook delay is noise on a 15-min bar.

nodes.label: Multi-exchange arbitrage
nodes.notes: WT has an arbitrage bot, but this is a different business model from the Algorithms branch. Defer.

nodes.label: Copy trading / signal selling
nodes.notes: WT supports it, but monetizing strategies is a distraction until they're proven live for ≥3 months.

nodes.label: Observation
nodes.notes: 11 Pine Script strategies exist with backtest results from prior development. Unknown: do these results survive realistic trading costs and webhook execution latency? Selection of 1–3 candidates for live deployment is required.

nodes.label: Hypothesis
nodes.notes: At least 3 of the 11 strategies will maintain profit factor ≥1.3 after applying slippage=3 ticks, commission=0.1%, and eliminating any repainting signals. Selected strategies will have ≥100 trades over 2+ years backtest data for statistical significance.

nodes.label: Null hypothesis (the 'stop' signal)
nodes.notes: If ZERO strategies maintain profit factor ≥1.3 after realistic costs, the entire deployment roadmap PAUSES until strategies are redesigned. This is the explicit pre-registered failure criterion.

nodes.label: Methodology
nodes.notes:
For each of 11 strategies set:
  slippage = 3
  commission_type = strategy.commission.percent
  commission_value = 0.1
  fill_orders_on_standard_ohlc = true

Run on max available historical data (20k bars on Premium). Record: net profit, profit factor, max DD, total trades, Sharpe, avg trade duration.

nodes.label: Robustness check
nodes.notes: Test across multiple market conditions: split data into trending vs ranging periods using date ranges. A strategy that only works in one regime is fragile. For request.security() strategies: verify NO repainting by running live for 24h and comparing to historical signals.

nodes.label: Analysis plan — composite ranking score
nodes.notes:
Composite score weights:
  40% × profit_factor
  30% × (1 / max_DD)
  20% × trade_count_normalized
  10% × diversity bonus

Select top 3. If <3 pass profit factor ≥1.3, deploy only those that do.

nodes.label: Alternative if top picks correlated
nodes.notes:
If top 3 by score are all correlated (e.g. all crypto momentum), substitute one with a mean-reversion or range-bound strategy even at lower score. Diversification beats marginal score gains.

User has range strategies (NQ/BTC 15M RANGE) and momentum strategies (BREAKOUT, RSI DIV) — pick across types.

nodes.label: Profit factor ≥ 1.3 after costs
nodes.notes: PF = sum of winning trades' profits divided by sum of losing trades' absolute losses. Threshold 1.3 means $1.30 won per $1.00 lost over the full sample. Below 1.3 after realistic costs = no edge after friction.

nodes.label: Max drawdown ≤ 25%
nodes.notes: Worst peak-to-trough decline over the full backtest. Above 25%, position-sizing math becomes hostile: at 1% risk per trade, 25% DD ≈ 25 consecutive losses or equivalent — emotionally and mathematically punishing.

nodes.label: Total trades ≥ 100
nodes.notes: Statistical significance threshold. Below 100 trades, results are noise. Above 100, you can trust win rate and average trade metrics within tolerable confidence.

nodes.label: Strategy-type diversity in top 3
nodes.notes:
Don't deploy 3 correlated strategies. If top 3 are all 'crypto trend-following on 4h', you have one bet, not three. Force diversity by:
• asset class (crypto vs futures vs gold)
• strategy type (trend vs mean-reversion vs range)
• timeframe (15m vs 1h vs 4h)

nodes.label: calc_on_every_tick = false
nodes.notes: Setting in strategy() declaration. If true, strategy recalculates on every tick during real-time, repainting historical bars. Always set to false for execution-grade strategies.

nodes.label: process_orders_on_close = false
nodes.notes: Setting in strategy() declaration. False = orders process on next bar's open. Safer for webhook execution: alert fires at bar close, order executes on next bar's open, matching real-world live behavior.

nodes.label: All request.security() use _src[1] + lookahead_on
nodes.notes:
Pattern:
  request.security(symbol, tf, _src[1],
                   lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on)

Without _src[1], higher-timeframe data uses the current (unclosed) HTF bar, causing silent forward-looking bias.

nodes.label: barstate.isconfirmed guard on entry conditions
nodes.notes:
Wrap entries:
  if myCondition and barstate.isconfirmed
      strategy.entry(...)

Belt-and-suspenders against intra-bar repainting.

nodes.label: Alert message JSON format
nodes.notes:
{
  "code": "Enter-Long",
  "orderType": "market",
  "amountPerTradeType": "quote",
  "amountPerTrade": 100,
  "leverage": 1
}

Embedded in each strategy.entry() / strategy.close() call as alert_message parameter.

nodes.label: Comment codes (case-sensitive!)
nodes.notes:
Enter-Long       — open long
Enter-Short      — open short
Exit-Long        — close long
Exit-Short       — close short
Exit-All         — flatten everything

Wrong case = silent failure. WT rejects but TV shows alert as fired.

nodes.label: TradingView alert message field
Webhook URL placement
nodes.notes:
TV Create Alert → Notifications tab → 'Webhook URL' field. Paste URL from your WunderTrading bot.

DO NOT also enable plain text notifications — that can cause duplicate signals.

nodes.label: Position sizing: delegate to WunderTrading
nodes.notes: Don't compute position size in Pine. Set amountPerTrade in the JSON (quote / base / percentage). WT handles conversion to exchange-specific contract sizes. Avoids the contract-size bug (remember the 126 BTC quantity issue).

nodes.label: Strategy archetype: swing vs flat-between
nodes.notes:
Always-in-position (long → short → long): use Swing Trade mode in WT bot config. Codes: Enter-Long, Enter-Short.

Flat-between strategies: use Exit-Long / Exit-Short codes explicitly. Don't rely on Enter-Short to close a long.

nodes.label: 24h chart test with alerts enabled
nodes.notes: Apply strategy to chart, enable alerts to 'Once Per Bar Close'. Set notification to 'Show popup' only (no webhook yet). After 24h check the alert log.

nodes.label: Cross-check log vs chart markers
nodes.notes: Every alert log entry should correspond to a strategy plot marker (arrow / triangle) on the chart. Every plot marker should have a log entry. Mismatch = alert not firing on some signals.

nodes.label: Verify JSON parses correctly
nodes.notes: Copy a few alert message texts from the log into a JSON validator (jsonlint.com). Catches stray quotes, missing braces, escape errors from Pine string interpolation.

nodes.label: Missed webhook (TV's 3-second timeout)
nodes.notes:
WHAT: TV posts to webhook URL. If WT doesn't respond in 3s, TV gives up. Signal silently lost.

CAUSE: WT server load, exchange API latency, network hiccup.

DETECTION: Daily reconciliation — count alerts in TV log vs signals received in WT log. Any gap = missed webhook.

FREQUENCY: Highest during volatility spikes.

nodes.label: Alert lag during volatility
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Signal fires 5+ seconds late during fast moves.

CAUSE: TV server load during major events.

DETECTION: Compare strategy chart marker time to alert log timestamp. Lag >10s on 15-min strategy = OK. Lag >60s = concerning.

MITIGATION: 15-min+ timeframes make seconds of lag invisible.

nodes.label: Duplicate alerts (both webhook + plain text enabled)
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Same signal received twice by WT, opens position twice or doubles size.

CAUSE: TV alert config has BOTH 'Webhook URL' and 'Show popup' / 'Email' notifications enabled.

DETECTION: WT bot log shows two entries within 1s. Position size = 2× expected.

FIX: Disable all non-webhook notifications in alert config.

nodes.label: Position desync (WT thinks flat, exchange has position)
nodes.notes:
WHAT: WT internal state says 'no position' but exchange actually has an open position. Next signal opens new position on top of existing.

CAUSE: Manual trade on same sub-account, exchange downtime during fill, partial fill that WT didn't reconcile.

DETECTION: Daily reconciliation script — exchange balance + open positions vs WT state. Any mismatch = desync.

FIX: Pause bot, manually flatten on exchange, re-sync WT.

nodes.label: Strategy recalc on script edit
nodes.notes:
WHAT: You edit a live strategy script (even adding a comment) and strategy recalculates from history. Can fire 'fake' alerts based on recalculation.

CAUSE: TV re-runs strategy from scratch on any code change.

FIX: NEVER edit a live strategy without first pausing the bot. Edit → verify alerts haven't fired falsely → unpause.

nodes.label: Partial fill drift
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Order for 10 BTC partially fills (8 BTC filled, 2 remaining), exchange cancels the rest. WT thinks 10 BTC; you actually have 8.

DETECTION: Daily reconciliation. Position size on exchange ≠ position size in WT log.

MITIGATION: Use market orders (less likely to partial-fill) or 'fill-or-kill' if bridge supports it.

nodes.label: Exchange downtime during scheduled maintenance
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Bybit/Binance schedule maintenance 1–2× per month, usually 30 min to 2 hours. During downtime, webhooks fail silently.

MITIGATION: Exchange-side TP/SL orders survive bridge downtime. Subscribe to exchange status pages. Don't deploy a new strategy in the 24h before scheduled maintenance.

nodes.label: Manual override of the bot (the human failure mode)
nodes.notes:
WHAT: You see the bot do something you don't like, manually close the trade. WT state now wrong, next reconciliation shows desync.

WHY THIS IS THE BIGGEST RISK: Most retail algo failures are psychological, not technical. The bot is doing what you told it; you second-guess it.

MITIGATION: If you don't trust it, paper longer. Don't deploy live what you'd manually override.
